note: Claims-first draft register for Spec 040, generated alongside spec.md from design D-25 (PR #195 portfolio, read in full) and the Spec 025 / Phase-140 / Phase-385 record, under the owner's 2026-10-20 bundle decision (gazetteer act first, published determinations only; D-25 follows). DRAFT: the AEE lifecycle hooks have not run on this register; they are a freeze gate (the Spec 035 ordering), and any recovery rounds at the freeze act will be recorded in aee/ and advance this version. Draft-stage self-checks (dependency integrity over this register; the cited-record facts) are pinned by backend/tests/test_spec040_freeze.py. Recovery at the freeze act of 2026-10-24 (round 1, 0.5-draft -> 0.6-draft): every evidence item gained an independent_of declaration naming the register's other evidence sources (separate documents, independently inspectable); the heads of F040-C03, F040-C05, F040-C06 and F040-C11 were restated as single propositions, each draft head carried verbatim into its claim's boundary with its remaining clause governed there - no proposition was dropped. Round 1's hooks (aee 1.5.3, lenient load, evidence verification off, no ledger) had returned 41 failure modes: 22 independence_unmodeled (one per evidence item), 4 coverage_gap irreducibility challenges (the four restated heads), 15 FR-2.3 draft-cap records; minimum propagated confidence 0.695. Recovery round 2 at the same act (0.6-draft -> 0.7-draft): F040-C11's head restated a second time as the single upper-bound condition (its first restated head is carried in its boundary); seven claims (F040-C07, C08, C09, C10, C12, C14, C15) each gained a second evidence item from a distinct record that states the claimed proposition (the Phase-385 report; the Spec 025 design record; the D-25 design source; the Spec 025 Phase-140 freeze record), and every independent_of declaration was recomputed against the enlarged source set. Round 2's hooks had returned 16 failure modes: 15 FR-2.3 draft-cap records and one coverage_gap challenge on F040-C11; eight claims stood below the 0.70 threshold at 0.695 - the seven single-evidence claims on their direct scores and F040-C11 by propagation from F040-C08.

claims.text: An outcome under Spec 040 states only whether the G1 site association survives coarse chronology control on the ICIT-lineage layer.
boundary: Scope claim for the whole spec. The claim under test is STUDY-SPEC-025/G1 as recorded by Phase-140 and Phase-385. What any sign means, whether people moved, and every PRED-2026 question are outside this spec. It does not govern the dependency gate (C02), the assignment discipline (C04), or the computations (C05-C08), which are stated separately.
alternatives: A chronology-controlled repertoire result may be read as evidence about language, dialects as peoples, or population movement.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 040 outcome statement claiming more than the bounded G1 consequence on the ICIT-lineage layer defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: A chronology-controlled repertoire result may be read as evidence about language, dialects as peoples, or population movement.
metadata.verdict_rule: A Spec 040 product makes a bounded G1 statement only.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C01 states the scope of every outcome; C15 states how outcomes are recorded and labelled. A statement inside scope is exactly one recorded as C15 requires. Neither negates the other.

evidence.description: Spec 025: G1's design, verdict rule, and the chronology rider carried in its freeze records
Phase-140 results: G1 SUPPORTED under composition and preservation control, chronology not controlled

claims.text: Spec 040 cannot be frozen until Spec 039's executed period labels exist in the frozen site-period form this spec consumes.
boundary: The dependency claim (spec section 1). It requires Spec 039 executed, its freeze digest and outcome merged, and a hash-pinned machine-readable assignment artifact at site-period resolution with citations and contested flags. A site-level occupation label alone does not satisfy it. It does not govern how assignments are applied at execution (C04) or the execution-stage thinness gate (C12).
alternatives: The 205-row chronology spine, or a site-level gazetteer label, is already enough to place inscriptions in period strata.
falsification_tests: A Spec 040 freeze record that names no merged Spec 039 execution, no assignment-artifact SHA-256, or only site-level labels defeats this claim and bars the freeze.

metadata.strongest_rival: The 205-row chronology spine, or a site-level gazetteer label, is already enough to place inscriptions in period strata.
metadata.verdict_rule: No frozen Spec 039 labels in consumable form, no Spec 040 freeze: the state is NOT-YET-TESTABLE at the dependency gate.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C02 governs the freeze-time dependency; C12 governs the execution-time thinness closure. The two gates run at different stages over different quantities and are consistent by construction. Neither negates the other.

evidence.description: Spec 027 section 6.2: the gazetteer unit, the program_period_assignment field, and its reservation to a governed act
Spec 030 outcome: the extended spine is 205 traced dated-context rows and Q6 remains NOT-YET-TESTABLE on it

claims.text: The primary test's base population is the Phase-137 population reproduced exactly.
boundary: The population claim (spec section 6.1). Base population: 5,410 inscriptions at the 7 Phase-137 eligible sites from the pinned layer; sign columns fixed from that full population (count at least 10, rarer pooled to OTHER, placeholders 000/999 excluded). The analysis population is the assigned subset under C04; the column set is not re-derived on it. It does not govern period assignment (C04) or inference (C06-C07). Draft head carried verbatim: 'The primary test's base population and sign columns are the Phase-137 population and profile configuration reproduced exactly.' The sign-column clause of the draft head is governed with the population clause by this claim: the sign columns are the Phase-140 profile configuration, fixed from the full base population and never re-derived on the assigned subset (DD-040-4).
alternatives: The population or sign columns could be rebuilt on the assigned subset for convenience.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 040 product whose base population differs from 5,410 inscriptions at the 7 recorded sites, or whose sign columns are re-derived on the assigned subset, defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: The population or sign columns could be rebuilt on the assigned subset for convenience.
metadata.verdict_rule: The Phase-137 population and columns govern; the assigned subset changes rows, never the profile's columns.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C03 fixes the rows and columns the test starts from; C05 fixes the strata the permutation respects. The two are consistent by construction: C05 crosses C03's population with the assignment of C04. Neither negates the other.

evidence.description: Phase-140 results: population 5,410, the 7 eligible sites, and the profile configuration asserted against Phase-137
Phase-140 freeze record: the population, profile table, and statistic configuration fixed for G1

claims.text: An inscription enters a primary period stratum only through a unique uncontested published-determination mapping in the frozen Spec 039 artifact.
boundary: The assignment claim (spec section 4). The mapping is keyed at site-period resolution over the inscription's recorded local chronological label; contested-only, ambiguous, missing, and transitional mappings leave the inscription UNASSIGNED in the primary. A site occupation label, a site radiocarbon date, the Phase-139 chron_band, and analyst judgement never place an inscription. It does not govern the contested sensitivity (C13), which uses the frozen sensitivity labels.
alternatives: An inscription may inherit its site's period label, or be placed from the site's dated contexts.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 040 primary stratum containing an inscription placed by site-label inheritance, by a spine date, by chron_band, or without a unique uncontested frozen mapping defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: An inscription may inherit its site's period label, or be placed from the site's dated contexts.
metadata.verdict_rule: Unique uncontested frozen mapping, or UNASSIGNED: no third route exists in the primary.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C04 states how an inscription is placed; C13 states how contested placements enter the sensitivity. The two are consistent by construction: the sensitivity is the only place a contested mapping is used. Neither negates the other.

evidence.description: Spec 027 section 6.2/6.5: source assertions are preserved with their scheme and conflicts, never silently harmonised
The 205-row extended spine: dated sample/context assertions by site, the support record the assignment artifact may cite

claims.text: The primary permutation holds period fixed jointly with the Spec 025 control strata.
boundary: The strata claim (spec sections 4 and 6.2). The stratum key is composition_stratum | preservation_class | period_stratum over the assigned population; site labels move only inside a stratum. Period enters by stratification, not as a regression covariate or matching score. It does not govern the statistic computed under the permutation (C06) or the interval estimator (C07). Draft head carried verbatim: 'The primary permutation respects composition, preservation, and period strata jointly.' The control strata named in the draft head are composition and preservation (the Phase-140 strata), with period added by this spec as the third stratum (DD-040-2).
alternatives: Period could be added as a covariate, or controlled by comparing period-specific tables, instead of stratifying the permutation.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 040 primary run that permutes a site label across a composition, preservation, or period boundary defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: Period could be added as a covariate, or controlled by comparing period-specific tables, instead of stratifying the permutation.
metadata.verdict_rule: One added stratification, nothing else changed: composition x preservation x period.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C05 fixes the exchangeability structure; C06 fixes the statistic and p-value computed under it, and C07 the interval. Each governs a different object and none restates another. Neither negates the other.

evidence.description: Phase-140 freeze record: site labels permuted within composition x preservation strata, UNRECORDED retained as a level
Spec 040 section 6.2: the stratum key with period added, carried from design D-25

claims.text: The primary statistic follows the Phase-140 configuration.
boundary: The inference claim (spec section 6.2). Pearson chi-square of the site x sign table as the divergence statistic; p = (1 + #{chi2_perm >= chi2_obs}) / (1 + B); Fisher-Yates via shuffle; no asymptotic p-value. The permutation p is reported with the outcome; under DD-040-1 it does not by itself mint the verdict, which C08-C11 assign from the interval. It does not govern the interval estimator (C07). Draft head carried verbatim: 'The primary statistic and permutation follow the Phase-140 configuration with 9,999 shuffles under seed 20261009.' The permutation clause of the draft head is governed with the statistic clause by this claim: the primary permutation runs 9,999 shuffles under seed 20261009 (spec section 6.2).
alternatives: A model-based test, an asymptotic p-value, or a different seed or shuffle count could be substituted.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 040 primary product computed with a different statistic, shuffle count, seed, or p formula defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: A model-based test, an asymptotic p-value, or a different seed or shuffle count could be substituted.
metadata.verdict_rule: The Phase-140 machinery, exactly: chi-square, B = 9,999, seed 20261009, the recorded p formula.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C06 computes the permutation companion; C07 computes the governing interval. The two are consistent by construction: the verdict mapping of C08-C11 reads C07's interval and reports C06's p beside it. Neither negates the other.

evidence.description: Phase-140 freeze record: statistic, B, seed, and p formula frozen for G1
Phase-140 results: the recorded permutation quantities the regression of section 7 must reproduce

claims.text: The governing effect interval is the Phase-385 v2 basic bootstrap interval for Cramer's V.
boundary: The interval claim (spec section 6.3). Inscriptions are resampled with replacement within the primary strata, stratum sizes preserved, B = 4,999, seed 20261012; both percentile and basic intervals are reported and the basic interval [2V - q97.5, 2V - q2.5] governs. It does not govern the margin the interval is judged against (C08).
alternatives: The percentile interval, or a fresh interval method, could govern instead.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 040 margin adjudication that uses the percentile interval, a different resampling unit, B, seed, or interval form defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: The percentile interval, or a fresh interval method, could govern instead.
metadata.verdict_rule: The basic bootstrap interval governs, exactly as Phase-385 v2 established for this result family.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C07 produces the governing interval; C08 states the margin it is read against. The two are consistent by construction: C08 judges the quantity C07 computes. Neither negates the other.

evidence.description: Phase-385 results v2: stratified bootstrap, B = 4,999, seed 20261012, basic interval governing over the percentile interval
Phase-385 report: the v2 stratified basic bootstrap interval is the governing interval for this result family, with the percentile interval reported beside it

claims.text: The practical margin for the chronology-controlled effect is Cramer's V = 0.10.
boundary: The margin claim (spec section 6.4). The margin is the Spec 026 / Phase-385 declared practical floor for this result family, carried unchanged; it is a floor on the governing interval, not on the point estimate and not on the permutation p. It does not govern which outcome an interval position produces (C09-C11).
alternatives: The margin could be re-set after the interval is seen, or read off the point estimate.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 040 adjudication against a margin other than V = 0.10, or against the point estimate instead of the governing interval, defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: The margin could be re-set after the interval is seen, or read off the point estimate.
metadata.verdict_rule: V = 0.10, declared before any outcome, judged on the basic interval.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C08 states the line; C09, C10, and C11 state the three mutually exclusive consequences of the interval's position relative to it. Each consequence claim governs one position only. Neither negates the other.

evidence.description: Phase-385 results: margin_v = 0.1 declared before the run, governing interval the basic bootstrap
Phase-385 report: 'Margin declared before any run: Cramer's V = 0.10' - the declared practical floor for this result family

claims.text: A governing interval lying entirely above 0.10 retires the chronology rider by appended record.
boundary: The supported consequence (spec section 6.4). It requires the basic interval's lower bound strictly above 0.10 after every gate has passed. The retirement is prospective and append-only: G1 reads SUPPORTED under control, chronology included, from that date; historical rider-carrying statements are not edited. It does not govern the straddle or below-margin consequences (C10-C11).
alternatives: A strong permutation p alone, or a point estimate above the margin, could retire the rider.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 040 record that retires the rider without a governing basic interval entirely above 0.10 defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: A strong permutation p alone, or a point estimate above the margin, could retire the rider.
metadata.verdict_rule: SUPPORTED - CHRONOLOGY CONTROLLED iff the governing interval lies entirely above 0.10.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C09 governs one interval position (entirely above the margin); C10 and C11 govern the other two. The three are mutually exclusive by construction and together exhaust the positions. Neither negates the other.

evidence.description: Phase-385 verdict: the governing basic CI [0.1838, 0.2102] lies entirely above the 0.10 floor, with the rider retained because chronology was not controlled
Spec 025: G1's design, verdict rule, and the chronology rider every G1 statement carries - the rider this consequence retires

claims.text: A governing interval straddling 0.10 restates G1 as a period-confounded association by appended record.
boundary: The weakened consequence (spec section 6.4): lower bound at or below 0.10 and upper bound above 0.10. G1 is weakened, not contradicted: it remains supported under composition and preservation control and is not established under chronology control, with the drop from the Phase-385 interval reported. It does not govern the entirely-above or entirely-at-or-below positions (C09, C11).
alternatives: A straddling interval could still be announced as supported with a caveat.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 040 record that announces a straddling interval as SUPPORTED - CHRONOLOGY CONTROLLED, or as contradicted at the margin, defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: A straddling interval could still be announced as supported with a caveat.
metadata.verdict_rule: WEAKENED - RIDER CONFIRMED AS MATERIAL iff the governing interval straddles 0.10.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C10 governs the straddle position only; C09 and C11 govern the positions on either side. The three are mutually exclusive by construction. Neither negates the other.

evidence.description: Phase-385 report: an interval crossing the declared margin is inconclusive at that margin, the discipline this consequence carries
Phase-385 report: the governing basic interval read against the declared V = 0.10 floor - the precedent for judging an interval against the margin

claims.text: An interval whose upper bound does not exceed the margin contradicts the chronology-controlled form of G1.
boundary: The contradicted consequence (spec section 6.4): upper bound at or below 0.10 after every gate has passed. It defeats the claim that the site association survives holding time fixed, at the declared practical margin. It does not assert that no site association exists in any form, and it does not alter Phase-140's differently-controlled result. It does not govern the straddle position (C10). Draft head carried verbatim: 'A governing interval lying entirely at or below 0.10 contradicts the chronology-controlled form of G1 at the declared margin.' In the restated head, 'the margin' is the declared margin V = 0.10 (F040-C08) and the interval is the governing basic bootstrap interval (F040-C07). Second restatement at the same act: 'An interval entirely at or below the margin contradicts the chronology-controlled form of G1.' - the disjunctive form restated as the single upper-bound condition spec section 6.4 states.
alternatives: An interval at or below the margin could be reported as merely weaker support.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 040 record that reports an entirely at-or-below-margin interval as supported or only weakened defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: An interval at or below the margin could be reported as merely weaker support.
metadata.verdict_rule: CONTRADICTED AT THE DECLARED MARGIN iff the governing interval lies entirely at or below 0.10.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C11 governs the entirely-at-or-below position only; C09 and C10 govern the other positions. The three are mutually exclusive by construction. Neither negates the other.

evidence.description: Phase-385 results: the margin adjudication form for this result family, basic interval against the 0.10 floor
Phase-140 results: the differently-controlled primary result that stands as its own design's record

claims.text: A failed margins gate closes the execution NOT-YET-TESTABLE with no outcome quantity computed.
boundary: The thinness claim (spec section 5). The gate requires each coarse period to retain assigned inscriptions from at least 5 distinct sites, the unassigned share at most 40 percent, and at least 1,000 permutable inscriptions under the primary strata (the third arm is DD-040-6, proposed at this draft). On failure the margins are the outcome record; G1 and its rider stand unchanged. It does not govern the freeze-time dependency gate (C02).
alternatives: A thin design could proceed anyway and let the interval speak for itself.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 040 execution that computes a profile outcome, permutation, or interval after a margins-gate failure defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: A thin design could proceed anyway and let the interval speak for itself.
metadata.verdict_rule: Gate failure is NOT-YET-TESTABLE, reported with its margins, and is not a verdict on G1.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C12 governs the execution-stage gate; C02 governs the freeze-stage gate. The two run in sequence over different quantities and are consistent by construction. Neither negates the other.

evidence.description: Spec 040 section 5: the margins gate, its three arms, and the NOT-YET-TESTABLE closure

Design D-25 (read in full at draft): the margins gate's first two arms - at least 5 sites in each period stratum, and more than 40% of rows unassignable closes the design - and its too-thin closure, whose word this spec governs as NOT-YET-TESTABLE (DD-040-5)

claims.text: Contested period mappings enter only the labelled sensitivity, under the sensitivity labels Spec 039 froze for them.
boundary: The contested claim (spec sections 4.4 and 8.1). The primary excludes contested mappings (C04); the sensitivity includes them under their frozen sensitivity labels, with all other rules unchanged, and reports its quantities beside the primary's. If no unique sensitivity label was frozen for a mapping, the sensitivity is NOT ESTIMABLE for it. The sensitivity mints no verdict and cannot change the primary outcome.
alternatives: Contested assignments could be silently kept in the primary, or silently dropped everywhere.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 040 product that uses a contested mapping in the primary, omits the contested-included sensitivity without a NOT ESTIMABLE record, or lets the sensitivity move the verdict defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: Contested assignments could be silently kept in the primary, or silently dropped everywhere.
metadata.verdict_rule: Contested mappings: excluded from the primary, included in the labelled sensitivity, both computations reported.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C13 governs the sensitivity use of contested mappings; C04 governs their exclusion from the primary. The two are consistent by construction: together they are the two-computation posture. Neither negates the other.

evidence.description: Spec 030 outcome: contested rows are neither silently dropped nor silently kept; both computations are reported
Spec 027 section 6.5: competing chronology assertions are preserved and any analysis names its scenario

claims.text: Leave-one-site-out computations under Spec 040 are stability readings that mint no verdicts.
boundary: The LOSO claim (spec sections 8.2-8.3). Every analysis site is dropped in turn and the primary quantities recomputed on the remaining assigned inscriptions; the Harappa drop is named in the headline sensitivity paragraph, or recorded NOT APPLICABLE if Harappa is not an analysis site. A subset that cannot support the effect is reported NOT ESTIMABLE for that subset. No LOSO result changes the section 6.4 outcome.
alternatives: A leave-one-site-out failure could overturn the primary outcome, or be omitted from the report.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 040 product that lets a LOSO result change the primary outcome, or that omits a computable LOSO member or the named drop-Harappa reading, defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: A leave-one-site-out failure could overturn the primary outcome, or be omitted from the report.
metadata.verdict_rule: LOSO and drop-Harappa are reported stability readings only; the primary outcome is already decided.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C14 governs the site-drop sensitivities; C13 governs the contested sensitivity. Each governs a different sensitivity and neither can move the primary outcome. Neither negates the other.

evidence.description: Spec 025 section 5: leave-one-site-out members are sensitivity analyses of an already-decided test and mint no verdicts of their own
Spec 025 Phase-140 freeze record: the sensitivity panel is EXPLORATORY and pre-declared; no sensitivity mints the verdict

claims.text: Every Spec 040 outcome is recorded by dated append under the ICIT-lineage label with its assignment census attached.
boundary: The record claim (spec sections 10-11). Outcomes land as appended dated entries in this spec's outcome record and the LEDGER; no frozen record (Spec 025, Phase-140, Phase-385, Spec 039) is edited. Every headline carries the lineage label, the outcome word, and the assignment census (assigned, unassigned, contested-excluded, and the Spec 039 artifact identity). It does not govern what the outcome is (C09-C12).
alternatives: A decisive result could be written back into the original G1 record so the page reads cleanly.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 040 consequence written by editing a frozen record, or any headline omitting the lineage label or the assignment census, defeats this claim.

metadata.boundary_confirmation: C15 governs the recording of whichever outcome C09-C12 produce; it does not restate any outcome's content. A recorded outcome inside scope (C01) is exactly one recorded as this claim requires. Neither negates the other.
